verdict.text: Spurs created the better chances (1.62 xG to 0.80) and deserved more than a draw.

howSpursPlayed: Spurs had 50.0% of the ball and 48.7% of the passing in the opposition half, against a season average of 58.8%.
They took 12 shots (3 on target) worth 1.62 xG, about 0.14 per shot; Man Utd had 12 shots worth 0.80.
The match changed after half-time: Spurs' xG difference went from +0.91 in the first half to -0.14 in the second.
Momentum: Spurs on top, 1–11'; Spurs on top, 13–25'; Man Utd on top, 62–69'.
In short: short, patient passing, took players on.

summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Man Utd's 4-2-3-1 (6 changes from the Aston Villa game).
Spurs created the better chances (1.62 xG to 0.80) and deserved more than a draw.

Compared with their other league games, Spurs spent less time in the opposition half (49% vs 69%), created better-quality chances (0.14 vs 0.07), had less of the ball (50% vs 61%), conceded less (0.80 xG vs 1.56 xG).
Solanke was the biggest attacking threat (0.73 xG + xA); Gray won the ball back most often (6 tackles won + interceptions).

phases.title: Build-up and possession

rows.label: Long balls, share of accurate passes

read: Spurs had 50% of the ball (season average 61%), completing 390 of 464 passes (84%).
49% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), well below their usual 69%. Territory was fairly shared.
52% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (204 own half, 186 opposition half): a balanced split between building and attacking.
Long balls made up 1.8% of accurate passes (well below the season's 3.8%), with 20% of long balls finding a teammate. Spurs built short and rarely went direct.

phases.title: Chance creation
read: 12 shots (3 on target) worth 1.62 xG, 0.14 per shot; the season average is 0.07 per shot, so the chances were better quality than usual.
8 shots came from inside the box and 4 from outside (33% from distance).
Spurs created 4 big chances and missed 3 (season average 2.2).
32 touches in Man Utd's box, in line with the season average of 30; Man Utd had 23 in Spurs' box.
Where the xG came from: open play 1.50 (96%), fast breaks 0.00, set pieces 0.06. 6 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).

phases.title: Finishing
read: Spurs scored 1 from 1.62 xG: 0.6 fewer than the chances were worth.
Shots on target were worth 1.38 xGOT against 1.62 xG before the shot: too many shots were off target or easy for the keeper.

phases.title: Out of possession
read: PPDA (estimated): 3.8 Man Utd passes in their own half per Spurs defensive action; season average 4.7. Lower means a more aggressive press, so this was a more intense press than usual.
17 tackles won and 18 interceptions (season averages 18.6 and 6.2); 12 clearances and 3 blocks.
Duels: Spurs won 50, Man Utd 61 (45% for Spurs); 56% of aerial duels won.
Man Utd managed 12 shots worth 0.80 xG (Spurs usually concede 1.56 xG) and 1 big chance.

phases.title: Transitions and set pieces
read: Fast breaks: Spurs had 0 shots on the break (0.00 xG); Man Utd had 2 (0.17 xG), against a season average of 1.2 shots conceded on the break.
Set pieces: 3 Spurs shots (0.06 xG, 0 goals); Man Utd 4 (0.23 xG, 0 goals). Corners: 4–4.

flow: First half: 0.96 xG for, 0.05 against (0–0). Second half: 0.60 for, 0.74 against (1–1). The balance shifted away from Spurs after half-time.
Spells on top (momentum index): Spurs 1–11'; Spurs 13–25'; Man Utd 62–69'.
73' Man Utd goal: Mbeumo from open play (assisted) (xG 0.10).
90+2' Spurs goal: Solanke from open play (assisted) (xG 0.23).
Spurs played with ten men after Bentancur's red card (78'); figures after that point reflect the numbers difference.
